questions.q: Which receipt routing method receives and puts away material in a single transaction, with no separate inspection step?
options: Direct delivery
Inspection required
Standard receipt
Express approval
questions.explain: Direct delivery receives and puts material away in one transaction, the fastest path, with no formal inspection.

questions.q: Why does LTV Manufacturing route the PB-4400 bearing through inspection required instead of direct delivery?
options: Because inspection is mandatory for every item in Oracle Fusion Cloud
Because a defective bearing in a production line motor risks costly downtime or equipment damage, making inspection worthwhile relative to its cost
Because Meridian Bearing Supply Co. requires it contractually for all customers
Because the bearing is a service item rather than a goods item
questions.explain: Routing is a risk-based decision configured per item: a critical mechanical part like this bearing justifies the cost of inspection given what a defect could cause.

questions.q: During inspection, what disposition can an inspector record for received material?
options: Only "accept" is possible - rejection does not exist in Oracle Fusion Receiving
The inspector can only reject; acceptance requires a separate approval workflow
Accept, reject, or a split disposition if only part of the shipment passes
The disposition is always determined automatically with no human review
questions.explain: An inspector can accept, reject, or split the disposition between accepted and rejected quantities based on what they find.

questions.q: Is receipt routing applied the same way to every item a company buys?
options: Yes, routing is a single global setting that applies identically to all items
Yes, but only for service purchase orders
No, routing can only be set by the supplier, never the buying company
No, routing is typically configured per item or per order, so a low-risk item could use direct delivery while a critical part uses inspection required
questions.explain: Routing decisions are made per item (or per order), allowing different risk levels to be handled with different routing methods.

questions.q: What is the outcome of inspection for LTV's shipment of 50 bearings in this course's main scenario?
options: All 50 units are rejected and returned to Meridian
Only 25 units pass; the rest are rejected
All 50 units pass inspection cleanly and are accepted in full
Inspection is skipped entirely for this shipment
questions.explain: In this course's clean, main-path scenario, the full shipment of 50 bearings passes inspection and is accepted in full.
